interest: Protecting Issei who aided the U.S. from Japanese treason laws, and Korea's collaborator purge.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.04417), filed under Japanese judicial affairs concerning offenses against the government, treason, and lèse-majesté between February 1946 and April 1949, consists of two distinct postwar records addressing legal retribution for wartime actions. The first part (February–May 1946) documents an initiative launched by Secretary of the Interior Harold L. Ickes requesting that the State Department secure legal immunity from prosecution under Articles 81 through 87 of the 1923 Criminal Code of Japan for Japanese resident aliens in the United States who supported the American war effort in military, intelligence, language teaching, agricultural, and industrial roles. State Department legal and geographic officers evaluated the proposal, concluding that while an amnesty could legally be imposed on Japan during Allied occupation or incorporated into the peace settlement, protecting these individuals once Japan regained sovereignty would be practically unenforceable. The second part (April 1949) consists of an incoming airgram from the American Mission in Seoul reporting on South Korea's ongoing investigations and arrests of alleged pro-Japanese collaborators under the National Traitors Act, detailing specific allegations against dozens of former colonial officials, detectives, police torturers, Privy Councillors, and wartime industrialists.

subfiles.about: Secretary of the Interior Harold L. Ickes appeals to Secretary of State James F. Byrnes to secure legal immunity against Japanese treason laws for Japanese resident aliens in the United States who aided the American war effort.
subfiles.from: Harold L. Ickes, Secretary of the Interior
subfiles.summary: Ickes asks Byrnes to protect Japanese aliens who aided the U.S. war effort from prosecution under Japan's treason laws, since U.S. law barred their naturalization.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Interior Harold L. Ickes to Secretary of State James F. Byrnes regarding immunity for Japanese resident aliens
subfiles.to: James F. Byrnes, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: English translation of Articles 81 through 87 of the 1923 Criminal Code of Japan defining capital and penal offenses against the state, treason, and wartime assistance to enemy powers.
subfiles.summary: English translation of Articles 81–87 of Japan's 1923 Criminal Code on aiding the enemy, enclosed with Ickes's letter.
subfiles.title: Enclosure 502: Articles 81 to 87, Criminal Code of Japan (1923)

subfiles.about: Assistant Legal Adviser William W. Bishop, Jr. advises on the legal validity and practical limits of compelling Japan to grant amnesty to Japanese resident aliens who assisted the United States.
subfiles.from: William W. Bishop, Jr., Assistant Legal Adviser (Le), Department of State
subfiles.summary: Bishop says the U.S. could demand an amnesty for Japanese aliens who aided it, but doubts it would hold after the occupation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Assistant Legal Adviser Bishop to Mr. Turner on amnesty for Japanese resident aliens
subfiles.to: William T. Turner, Division of Japanese Affairs (JA), Department of State

subfiles.about: William T. Turner requests the Legal Adviser's opinion on whether the United States can properly interfere with Japan's sovereign right to punish treason.
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, Division of Japanese Affairs (JA), Department of State
subfiles.summary: Turner asks Bishop whether the U.S. can legally stop Japan from punishing aliens who aided the American war effort.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Mr. Turner to Mr. Bishop regarding feasibility of Japanese alien immunity proposal
subfiles.to: William W. Bishop, Jr., Assistant Legal Adviser (Le), Department of State

subfiles.about: The Department of State responds to the Department of the Interior detailing the legal authority and practical challenges of securing postwar immunity from Japanese treason laws.
subfiles.from: Under Secretary of State (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: The Under Secretary tells Chapman the occupation can protect Japanese aliens who aided the U.S., but not once Japan regains sovereignty.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Under Secretary of State to Acting Secretary of the Interior Oscar L. Chapman regarding immunity for Japanese aliens
subfiles.to: Oscar L. Chapman, Acting Secretary of the Interior

subfiles.about: The American Mission in Seoul transmits an annotated list of individuals arrested or interrogated by the Special Investigation Board under the National Traitors Act for pro-Japanese collaboration.
subfiles.summary: Seoul airgram on arrests under South Korea's National Traitors Act through March 31, 1949, naming 41 suspected collaborators.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-119 from Seoul on arrests and investigations under the National Traitors Act
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Department of State
